modules.name: CSV Import
modules.description: Module to import MISP attributes from a csv file.

metadata.author: Christian Studer
metadata.name: CSV Import
metadata.description: Module to import MISP attributes from a csv file.
metadata.features:
In order to parse data from a csv file, a header is required to let the module know which column is matching with known attribute fields / MISP types.

This header either comes from the csv file itself or is part of the configuration of the module and should be filled out in MISP plugin settings, each field separated by COMMAS. Fields that do not match with any type known in MISP or are not MISP attribute fields should be ignored in import, using a space or simply nothing between two separators (example: 'ip-src, , comment, ').

If the csv file already contains a header that does not start by a '#', you should tick the checkbox 'has_header' to avoid importing it and have potential issues. You can also redefine the header even if it is already contained in the file, by following the rules for headers explained earlier. One reason why you would redefine a header is for instance when you want to skip some fields, or some fields are not valid types.
metadata.input: CSV format file.
metadata.output: MISP Event attributes

header.message:
Define the header of the csv file, with types (included in MISP attribute types or attribute fields) separated by commas.
For fields that do not match these types or that you want to skip, please use space or simply nothing between commas.
For instance: ip-src,domain, ,timestamp

has_header.message: Tick this box ONLY if there is a header line, NOT COMMENTED, and all the fields of this header are respecting the recommendations above.

special_delimiter.message: IF THE DELIMITERS ARE NOT COMMAS, please specify which ones are used (for instance: ";", "|", "/", "	" for tabs, etc).

modules.name: GoAML Export
modules.description: This module is used to export MISP events containing transaction objects into GoAML format.

metadata.author: Christian Studer
metadata.description: This module is used to export MISP events containing transaction objects into GoAML format.
metadata.name: GoAML Export
metadata.features:
The module works as long as there is at least one transaction object in the Event.

Then in order to have a valid GoAML document, please follow these guidelines:
- For each transaction object, use either a bank-account, person, or legal-entity object to describe the origin of the transaction, and again one of them to describe the target of the transaction.
- Create an object reference for both origin and target objects of the transaction.
- A bank-account object needs a signatory, which is a person object, put as object reference of the bank-account.
- A person can have an address, which is a geolocation object, put as object reference of the person.

Supported relation types for object references that are recommended for each object are the folowing:
- transaction:
	- 'from', 'from_my_client': Origin of the transaction - at least one of them is required.
	- 'to', 'to_my_client': Target of the transaction - at least one of them is required.
	- 'address': Location of the transaction - optional.
- bank-account:
	- 'signatory': Signatory of a bank-account - the reference from bank-account to a signatory is required, but the relation-type is optional at the moment since this reference will always describe a signatory.
	- 'entity': Entity owning the bank account - optional.
- person:
	- 'address': Address of a person - optional.
metadata.input: MISP objects (transaction, bank-account, person, legal-entity, geolocation), with references, describing financial transactions and their origin and target.
metadata.output: GoAML format file, describing financial transactions, with their origin and target (bank accounts, persons or entities).

The module takes an IP address attribute as input and answers from one of two sources:

metadata.description: Look up a SHA256 digest in the Malwagon sandbox and return the scans it already has for it.
metadata.name: Malwagon Lookup
requirements: A Malwagon API key with the read scope.
metadata.features:
The module takes a sha256 or filename|sha256 attribute and asks Malwagon which analyses it already holds for that digest. The lookup is free and answers immediately, so it is safe to use on hover: no sample leaves the MISP instance and no detonation quota is spent. Only the digest is sent.

Each analysis comes back as a sandbox-report object carrying the verdict, the score and a permalink to the report, referenced from a file object for the sample. The verdict is translated into MISP's own vocabulary - a misp:threat-level tag, plus ioc:artifact-state where the verdict is conclusive - rather than being passed through as a vendor string.

To detonate something Malwagon has never seen, use the Malwagon Submit module instead.
metadata.input: A sha256 or filename|sha256 attribute.
metadata.output: A file object for the sample and one sandbox-report object per Malwagon analysis, with the verdict expressed as MISP taxonomy tags.

modules.name: Malwagon Submit
modules.description: Detonate a sample or a URL in the Malwagon sandbox and return the analysis.

metadata.author: Tolga Sezer
metadata.description: Detonate a sample or a URL in the Malwagon sandbox and return the analysis.
metadata.name: Malwagon Submit
requirements: A Malwagon API key with the submit scope.
metadata.features:
The module takes an attachment, malware-sample or url attribute and detonates it in the Malwagon sandbox. A malware-sample arrives zip-encrypted with the password infected and is unpacked before submission.

A file is looked up by its SHA256 first. If Malwagon has already analysed that digest the existing analysis is returned, which is free, instant, and spends no detonation quota; set always_submit to force a fresh detonation instead. The module then polls the scan until it finishes or until poll_timeout seconds have passed, and returns what it has either way, so a long detonation gives back a permalink rather than an error.

This module submits the sample itself to a third party, so it is deliberately expansion-only and never runs on hover. Submission is blocked when the attribute carries a TLP tag more restrictive than max_tlp, and scans are created private unless private is set to false.

The sandbox image is chosen by the platform from the sample; on the free and community tiers the analysis virtual machine has no internet access at all, which is structural rather than a quota, so network-dependent samples will look inert there.
metadata.input: An attachment, malware-sample or url attribute.
metadata.output: A file object for the sample and a sandbox-report object for the Malwagon analysis, with the verdict expressed as MISP taxonomy tags.

metadata.name: PTR Classification
requirements: ptrclassify and dnspython Python libraries; DNS access for IP lookups
metadata.features:
IPv4 and IPv6 attributes are reverse-resolved and every distinct PTR hostname is classified locally using ptrclassify's built-in rules, retaining the queried address to detect IP-encoded naming. Hostname and domain attributes are classified directly, without DNS or an API key. Matching ptrclassify taxonomy tags are added to the queried attribute, retaining its UUID and existing tags, and to PTR answers in a `dns-record` object. One `ptrclassify` object per hostname holds the classification labels, confidence, evidence, rule IDs and potential location hints. Repeated classification fields share the machine tag as their attribute comment; location fields share a rule-ID/code comment. Classification objects reference the queried attribute and, for IP lookups, the DNS object. No match returns an object with `matched=0` without adding tags. Configure `nameserver` to use a specific DNS server; otherwise the system resolver is used. DNS lookups have a five-second lifetime.

Classification is heuristic: PTR names are operator-controlled, and inferred locations are hints, not verified geolocation. Hover displays the enrichment; importing the expansion applies the returned tags in MISP. Enable the ptrclassify taxonomy in MISP to manage these tags, and install the ptrclassify MISP object template. The module bundles the template so it also works with PyMISP versions that do not yet include it.
metadata.input: An ip-src, ip-dst, domain|ip, hostname or domain attribute.
metadata.output: The tagged input attribute, one ptrclassify object per hostname, and a dns-record object for IP lookups.

metadata.name: SoChain
metadata.features:
Query the SoChain API v3 for a btc attribute or a coin-address object. A btc attribute is looked up on Bitcoin. A coin-address object is looked up on the network named by its symbol (BTC, LTC, DOGE or ZEC); without a symbol, the network is the first of Bitcoin, Litecoin, Dogecoin and Zcash on which SoChain says the address is valid.

The result is a coin-address object with the balance, total received and sent, the number of transactions and the first and last activity, referencing the input. Recent counterparties are returned as coin-address objects linked with `paid` references (5 on hover, 50 when the magnifying glass is clicked), whose comments give the amount, transaction and block. When look-alike addresses sent the address dust to poison its history, each one is returned as a coin-address object that `impersonates` the address it copies.

No API key is needed for up to 2,500 lookups a day per IP. With a key from https://sochain.com/dashboard, lookups count against that account's plan.

metadata.author: Christian Studer
metadata.description: Expand vulnerabilities and CPEs with Vulnerability Lookup advisories and enrichment
metadata.name: Vulnerability Lookup
metadata.features:
Query vulnerability identifiers or CPEs. Import linked advisories, comments, bundles, sightings, storage metadata, EPSS scores and known-exploited assertions as related MISP content. Enable with_timeline to include dated milestones as an annotation.
api_url defaults to https://vulnerability.circl.lu (instance root, without /api). timeout defaults to 30 seconds per request (maximum 120). max_related defaults to 50 (0-100): it bounds alias lookup attempts, CPE results and each enrichment section. with_linked, with_comments, with_bundles, with_sightings, with_meta, with_epss and with_kev default to true; with_timeline defaults to false. Boolean options accept true/false or their string equivalents.
Unset options (null or blank strings from MISP) use their documented defaults. The request's top-level timeout limits total module execution independently of config.timeout.
CPE lookup uses cpe_source (default cvelistv5) and cpe_page (default 1). Results match vendor and product; exact version applicability must be checked. CPE search imports advisories from one bounded page; the optional community and priority lookups apply to vulnerability ID input.
Original advisory JSON is retained as a base64 payload; community, EPSS and KEV records retain JSON attachments. Unavailable optional data does not discard the advisory. The companion vulnerability-sighting, epss-score and known-exploited-vulnerability templates are bundled for compatibility with existing PyMISP releases.
metadata.input: Vulnerability or CPE attribute
metadata.output: Vulnerability, weakness, annotation, sighting, EPSS and KEV objects. Relationships are included in each object's ObjectReference list and in a deduplicated results.ObjectReference list, with source and target UUIDs and relationship types.
